name: Dual Sign Rank of Singletons
proof: Dual sign rank uses a fixed column set that is independent in every real sign realization; it is not sign rank of the transpose. By Claim 4 of Alon--Moran--Yehudayoff, such a column set is exactly an antipodally shattered set. On $k$ chosen coordinates the singleton traces are the $k$ unit vectors, together with zero if $k<n$. A single coordinate always represents its sole complementary pair. For $n=2$, both coordinates give only the pair $\{01,10\}$, so the value is one. For $n=3$, two coordinates represent both complementary pairs, but all three miss $\{000,111\}$, so the value is two. For $n\ge4$, three coordinates give zero and the three unit vectors, representing all four complementary pairs. No $k\ge4$ works, since at most $k+1<2^{k-1}$ traces are available. Thus the displayed values hold, including $n=1$.
references: \cite{alon2016sign}, Appendix E, Claim 4 (antipodal shattering and fixed-column universal independence).
